text:
Alice Chen: heads up — since 03:12 UTC we started seeing a pattern where requests fail after geo-dns failover to eu-west. Model servers return 502s intermittently. Appears tied to NAT/egress differences between regions.
Mateo Ruiz: saw the same. haproxy logs show lots of `connection reset by peer` and backend health flaps right after failover events. stack traces point to session sticky mismatch.
Priya Singh: reminder — cross-region egress is expensive for sustained traffic. If fallback routes send steady traffic to another region we could blow committed GPU egress budgets. Need cost guardrails in plan.
Jordan Li: quick hypothesis — when client goes to fallback region the source IP changes (new NAT pool) and our regional LB sticky keys use source IP for affinity, so requests route to different backend and KV cache misses -> 502s on some model instances.
oncall-bot: alert EG-1234 created (severity: medium) — cross-region egress failover causing 5xx burst
SRE-Triage: mitigation idea: slow down failover and prefer same-region pinning for sticky sessions. Reduce DNS TTL to 30s? actually we should increase TTL to avoid flapping while we stabilize. Also change geo-routing to require 3 consecutive health-check failures before failover.
Alice Chen: agree on longer stabilization window. Proposed immediate actions: 1) increase GeoDNS failover threshold to 3 fails / 30s 2) switch routing policy to 'region-pin with controlled fallback' 3) add header `x-redwood-origin-region` so services can detect cross-region requests 4) temporarily disable source-ip affinity for model-serving LBs and use cookie-based stickiness.
Mateo Ruiz: cookie-based stickiness will avoid NAT source-ip problems. Quick config snippet we can roll to HAProxy:
```
backend models
  cookie REDWOOD insert indirect nocache
  balance roundrobin
  server m1 10.0.1.4:8080 cookie m1 check
  server m2 10.0.1.5:8080 cookie m2 check
```
Jordan Li: also add a routing policy tweak: only allow cross-region fallback for stateless inference or during autoscaling events. For heavy KV-backed workloads keep strict region pinning. We'll need a per-route annotation.
Priya Singh: +1 on per-route policy. Also request finance tag on any cross-region egress so we can track cost during the canary. Logging: add metric `egress.bytes.cross_region` and a billing tag.
SRE-Triage: immediate mitigation steps I'm doing now: rolling config to disable source-ip affinity (canary 5% traffic), set geo-dns consecutive failures=3, increase fallback debounce to 45s. Will monitor for 30m.
Alice Chen: rollout plan for tomorrow (canary -> progressive):
- stage 0: deploy cookie stickiness to HAProxy in eu-west/us-east (5% traffic)
- stage 1: enable `x-redwood-origin-region` header and per-route fallback flags (10% traffic)
- stage 2: add finance egress tag + metrics (50% traffic)
- stage 3: full switch, preserve old config as quick rollback
(automation playbook will be in infra-runbooks/multi-region-egress.md)
Mateo Ruiz: monitoring: set alerts on 5xx spike, increased kv-cache-miss rate, cross_region_egress > 100MB/min. Dashboards PR coming.
Priya Singh: cost guard: cap daily cross-region egress at $X (placeholder) and trigger automated throttling / notify SRE when breached.
Jordan Li: we should also add a graceful fallback circuit: if fallback target reports >5% errors in 2m, route back to primary and mark fallback unhealthy for 10m.
Alice Chen: noted. Owners: Alice (rollout), Mateo (LB config), Jordan (routing policy), Priya (cost controls). Meeting to sync in 30m in #oncall-war-room.
SRE-Triage: executing canary now, will post status updates.
Mateo Ruiz: got it — monitoring panels up, watching haproxy and model health. :thumbsup:
Priya Singh: thanks team. If cost tags spike ping me immediately.
Alice Chen: ending thread — keep replies in this thread only for visibility. Will update with canary metrics in 10m.
